chunks: Beware of exaggeration regarding us; say that we are servants of God, and speak of our virtues as you wish.
Whoever loves us should act according to our actions and seek assistance through piety, for it is the best means of assistance in worldly and religious affairs.
Do not sit with those who find fault with us, and do not praise us before our enemies by openly showing our love, lest you humble yourselves before your kings.
Adhere to truthfulness, for it is a means of salvation; desire what is with God the Exalted, seek His obedience, and be patient in it.
How ugly it is for a believer to enter Paradise while his dignity is stripped away.
Do not rely solely on our seeking and intercession for you on the Day of Resurrection for what you have done.
Do not disgrace yourselves before your enemies on the Day of Resurrection, and do not deny your own rank with God for the sake of the lowly world.

Hold fast to what God has commanded you; between you and being delighted and seeing what you love is only the presence of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and what is with God is better and more permanent, and the glad tidings will come to him from God the Exalted, so his eye will be cooled and he will love to meet God.
Do not belittle your weak brethren, for God the Exalted will not unite the one who belittles a believer with that believer in Paradise unless he repents.
A believer should not make his brother seek out him when he knows his need.
Support one another, show affection, and give freely, and do not be like the hypocrite who describes what he does not do.

Get married, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever loves to follow my Sunnah should get married, for marriage is from my Sunnah.' And seek children, for I will be the most numerous of nations tomorrow because of you.
Feed your children with the milk of the adulteress and the insane woman, for milk transmits [qualities/illness].
Abstain from eating birds that do not have a beak, a spur, or a gizzard.
And beware of every beast of prey with fangs and every bird with claws.
And do not eat the spleen, for it is the house of spoiled blood.
And do not wear black, for it is the clothing of Pharaoh.
And beware of the glands in meat, for they stir the vein of leprosy.

Do not use analogy in religion, for there is in religion that which cannot be analogized, and there will come people who use analogy, and they are the enemies of religion, and the first to use analogy was Satan.
Do not wear rectangular shoes, for they are the shoes of Pharaoh, and he was the first to wear rectangular shoes.
Oppose the drinkers of intoxicants, and eat dates, for they contain a cure for diseases.
Follow the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), for he said: 'Whoever opens for himself a door of asking, God opens for him a door of poverty.'
Abound in seeking forgiveness to bring about sustenance, and hasten to do as much good as you can, so you may find it tomorrow.
Beware of argumentation, for it breeds doubt.

Whoever has a need from his Lord the Exalted should seek it at three times: a time on Friday, a time when the sun sets when the winds blow and the gates of heaven open and mercy descends and birds sing, and a time at the end of the night at the rising of dawn, for two angels call out: 'Is there any repentant one that repentance is accepted from him? Is there any beggar that he is given? Is there any one seeking forgiveness that he is forgiven? Is there any one seeking a need that it is granted to him?' So answer the caller of God.

And seek sustenance between the rising of dawn and the rising of the sun, for it is faster in seeking sustenance than striking the earth, and it is the time at which God divides sustenance among His servants.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical and practical teachings of Imam Ali regarding daily life and faith in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This comprehensive sermon, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, encapsulates the 'Four Hundred' teachings by balancing theological precision—specifically warning against *al-Ghulu* (exaggeration in the Imams' status)—with practical *fiqh* and *akhlaq*. It underscores the Shia principle that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is validated through righteous action and piety rather than mere verbal praise or reliance on intercession alone, while also providing specific legal rulings on diet, clothing, and social conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 27-3 I admonish you against boasting about us. You should say that we are servants of God, but you may state our virtues.
Whoever loves us should act as we do. You should seek the assistance of piety, since it is the best assistant in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.
Do not associate with those who try to find fault with us. Do not praise us in front of our enemies. Do not express our love publicly, since then you may become despised by the kings.
Adhere to righteousness since it will save you.Be inclined to what is near the Honorable the Exalted God. Try to obey God. Persevere in obeying God.
How awkward would it be for a believer to enter Paradise without dignity.
You should not just be hopeful of our intercession on your behalf on the Resurrection Day. You should make an effort yourself to do good deeds.
You should not disgrace yourself in front of your enemies in the Hereafter. You should not deny your own rank near God in front of your enemies for this lowly world.

You should forget about trying to get what others own due to God’s commands. Have you not heard that God’s Prophet (MGB) has informed us that what is near God is better and more permanent. Should a believer receive the glad tidings from the Honorable the Exalted God, he would be delighted and interested in visiting God.
Do not belittle your weak brethren. The Honorable the Exalted God will not unite whoever belittles a believer with that believer in Heaven, unless he repents.
You should help fulfill the needs of your brethren as soon as you realize that he needs something before he asks.
Be friends for each other. Be kind to each other. Give gifts to one another. Do not be like a hypocrite who says something, but doesn’t act accordingly.

Get married as this is a tradition of God’s Prophet (MGB). He (MGB) said, ‘Whoever likes to follow my traditions should get married, since getting married is one of my traditions.’ You should also try to have children, since then your large nation will be proud in the Hereafter.
You should not feed your babies with an adulterer’s milk or an insane woman’s milk, since milk could transfer a mother’s illness to the child.
You should not eat any birds which do not have a gizzard, a spur on its feet, or a craw .
You should not eat any wild animals that have canine teeth and or birds that have claws.
You should not eat a spleen since it spoils the blood.
You should not wear black clothes since that was how Pharaoh dressed.
You should not eat any meat glands since this may cause leprosy.
You should not make comparisons regarding religious affairs as that doesn’t hold. Those who do so are the enemies of the religion. It was Satan who did so first.
Do not wear rectangular shoes since Pharaoh’s shoes were that way. Pharaoh was the first person who wore such shoes.
You should oppose wine-drinkers. I advise you to eat dates since they are the cure of every pain.
You should obey the sayings of God’s Prophet (MGB) who said, ‘God will open a door of poverty to anyone who opens up the door of a question to himself. ’
You should ask God for forgiveness often, since that would expedite the arrival of your daily sustenance. You should rush to do good deeds, so that you may benefit from them in the Hereafter.
I admonish you against arguing because it causes doubt.

If you have any needs from the Honorable the Exalted Lord, you should choose any of the following three times to ask Him for it: sometime on Fridays; at the time of sunset; when the wind blows - that is at times when the gates of Heaven are opened and Mercy descends; when the birds sing and at the last hours of night when the dawn comes at which time two angels announce, ‘Is there anyone who repents whose repentance is accepted of him? Is there anyone begging for anything so that it be granted to him? Is there anyone asking for forgiveness so that he be forgiven? Is there anyone asking for anything to be given to him?’ and one responds, ‘Yes. Here I am! I am responding to the Supreme God’s invitation.’
Ask (God) for your share of daily bread from dawn until sunrise. This would be better than going around after work, since this is the time at which God divides his servants’ share of daily bread.
